pattern.top_pattern: CA spend is rising in acute hospital and rehab settings, concentrated in aftercare, electrolyte, trauma, and spine cases
pattern.what_is_impacting: CA PPO Local acute hospital and physical rehab admissions
key_driver_codes: Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC
Miscellaneous Disorders of Nutrition, Metabolism, and Fluids and Electrolytes with MCC
pattern.pattern_details: CA has a concentrated inpatient and post-acute cost increase across PPO Local acute hospital and physical rehab settings. The operational increase is reinforced by clinical concentration in aftercare, electrolyte disorders, and a smaller set of rare trauma and spine cases, with Good Samaritan Hospital appearing repeatedly. This looks less like broad-based inflation and more like a focused mix of placement, case complexity, and provider concentration.
pattern.why_it_matters: CA has enough scale and concentration to support joint UM, clinical, and network action rather than a broad statewide policy change.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Launch a joint CA review of aftercare and electrolyte admissions, validate whether rehab placement was appropriate, and assess provider-specific pricing and episode management at Good Samaritan Hospital.
pattern.validation_reason: Part of the CA increase includes rare small-count cases and an unmapped clinical bucket, so confirm coding and episode classification while reviewing placement and reimbursement.
evidence_summary: CA physical rehab added about $0.7M in mixed volume and unit-cost pressure, including 10 more admissions and about $16.0K higher paid per admit in Aftercare with CC/MCC.

CA acute hospital added about $0.8M in mixed and volume-led pressure, led by Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC at about $0.3M and Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC at about $0.2M.
Clinical case mix added about $0.9M from aftercare and electrolyte diagnoses, including ENC AFTERCARE FLW SURGERY NEOPLASM at about $0.3M and HYPO-OSMOLALITY AND HYPONATREMIA at about $0.2M.
Rare trauma and spine-related cases added about $0.9M, including several single-case episodes paid at roughly $40K to $175K per admit.
